### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `create-objectstack`, `objectstack-blank`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**52** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/create-objectstack/README.md`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `packages/create-objectstack/src/templates/blank/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sharingModel (symbol, 49 pages)`, `owner_id (literal, 46 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b293b2d5dc1e14ab9135e24aa60d64c0109ee227` — the merge of head `4bf5626c8c3c31086a4daee07ab7f5b1dce7997f` into base `f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b293b2d5dc1e14ab9135e24aa60d64c0109ee227 && git checkout b293b2d5dc1e14ab9135e24aa60d64c0109ee227
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba 4bf5626c8c3c31086a4daee07ab7f5b1dce7997f && git checkout -B drift-repro f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba && git merge --no-ff 4bf5626c8c3c31086a4daee07ab7f5b1dce7997f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f71d488d6f4d7181cc6e075eb956f92489fb87ba` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `973207caad6ea4b0cc064a1d29abc28222145f41`
Local-runs: none

PR #37428 (card #36945), declaration face, `Clause-②: no`. Read: the card body and all 11 card comments (ruling 7183516548, release 7183536185, re-claim 7187337406), the maintainer's own words in the card thread at 2026-11-26T08:58Z (「改」, 「仓库中的对象为什么要等发版本」, 「你可以落地啊」, read in the thread itself), card #37441, the PR body with Landing ops §C, the diff `origin/main...973207ca` (37 files, +898/−314), the check-runs on the head and the failed job's log. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Findings**

- M1 (must-fix) — The PR breaks a second gate that §C does not list: the release candidate's packed-tarball smoke. `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` lines 1183 to 1211 read `$APP_DIR/src/objects/note.object.ts` and then POST `{"title":"publish smoke"}` to that object. In pack mode the project is scaffolded by the repo-built `create-objectstack` (line 654), so after this PR the file is not there. The script runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 118), so the `readFileSync` throws and the smoke stops at "REST CRUD probes". `publish-smoke.yml` runs this after every Release run and reports it as the commit status `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` on the release branch head; that status is green today (last success 2026-11-26T08:53Z). It is the only gate that drives a fresh packed install through auth and CRUD before a publish, and the next publish is the first `19.0.0-next` cut. It is not a required context, so nothing stops the merge. This is read from the script, not run. §C says "One red is expected on this head", and the dev report's A3 says every `note` reference was removed or moved; both are wrong on this point, and the maintainer's 08:58Z word to land was given on a stated cost of one red. Fix: make the CRUD probe find the starter object in both modes (pack mode gets `company.object.ts` and a required `name`; registry mode scaffolds the published 18.6.0 template, which still has `note.object.ts` and `title`, until 19.0 GA). The script is not a governed path, so the fix can ride this PR with a fence amendment, or land first on its own card. Either way §C must name it before the PR lands.
- S1 (should-fix) — §C states the cost of the expected red too narrowly. The job stops at step 7, so steps 8 to 14 are skipped: the template's own `starter.test.ts`, the boot probe, the skills boundary, the pinned shape and both Docker legs. No other CI job runs `starter.test.ts` (this package's vitest excludes `src/templates/`). So until #37441 lands or a 19 prerelease is published, no CI run executes the new template's test or boots a generated project, on this PR or on any later PR that touches `packages/create-objectstack/**` or `docker/**`; a second template regression in that window is hidden behind the `color` refusal. #37441 is `pm:queue`, p2 and unclaimed. Say this in §C, and move #37441 ahead in the queue.
- S2 (should-fix) — The field-consumer note needs a card. The rule credits the column names of an object-form `relatedLists` entry to the object that declares the list, so a parent field that nothing displays stays silent when a child's related-list column has the same name. That is a missed finding at `os validate` and `os lint`, with a named probe (the PR's own control: 7 of 12 blank controls stay green until the helper drops the name from every related list). `withoutPlacement` in `starter-field-consumers.test.ts` now strips those columns on every object, which keeps the control honest today and also hides the defect from it; the card should narrow the helper when the rule is fixed. Filing is the seat's act at ACCEPT.
- S3 (should-fix) — The `generate.ts` comment needs a card too, as one family card and not a single-site one. The comment at `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts:295` names a file that no longer exists, and its claim is now partly false: the PR body says the style it describes "is unchanged", but `os g object` places a field with a per-field `group: 'details'` (pinned in `generate-scaffold-validates.test.ts:373` to 386 under "the generators write the starter's style"), and the starter now places every field through a group's `fields` list. Both spellings are valid; the #32153 promise of one dialect no longer holds for placement, and someone has to decide which way it goes. Same family, stale only: `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:1091` and `:1103` (a public transcript showing `my_app_note (2 fields, user)`), `init-scaffold-file-name-registry-parity.test.ts:36`, `platform-object-names.test.ts:42`, the header of `blank-template-console-disclosure.test.ts` (lines 26 to 28) and comments in `starter-comments-self-contained.test.ts`. The `note.object.ts` path strings in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` are fixtures that read no file and can stay. The two comments in `scaffold-e2e.yml` are already carried by #37441.
- N1 (nit) — The "two-line" platform-objects edit is two sites, each one line replaced by two (+4/−2 over two files).
- N2 (nit) — `namespacedLiteralRe` and the self-check `findStaleNamespacePrefixes` share one pattern, so they are blind to the same shapes. A dotted related-list name (`'blank_contact.company'`, the `object.field` form the spec allows) would be neither rewritten nor reported. The template has none today, and `objectstack validate` in the generated project would refuse it.
- N3 (nit) — The parity pin holds the object file set but not the view file set, and it pins the closing summary by matching `index.ts` source text, not printed output.

**1. Does the generated project equal the Starter's company and contact?** Yes, where ruling 7183516548 requires it. Read side by side with `starter_` spelled `blank_`: both objects, both view definitions and the four object menu entries are the same code; the differences are comments and the views' export form. Not carried, and declared: the Starter's dashboard entry, seed data, translations and the app's own name, label, icon and branding. `blank-template-starter-parity.test.ts` holds this with the TypeScript printer, comments removed.

`requiresObject` is the right guard for an 18.6.0 install. At tag `@objectstack/spec@18.6.0` the key exists on a navigation entry (`app.zod.ts:442`), `sys_task` and `sys_note` do not exist in `platform-objects`, and `validate-object-references.ts` answers an unknown platform-prefixed name with a warning, not an error. That matches the dev's measurement (validate passes with 7 warnings once the three shapes are stripped). The guard does not rescue the project: 18.6.0 refuses it earlier.

**What a user pays between this landing and the 19.0.0-next publish.** A user who runs `npm create objectstack` pays nothing, because they do not get this template. The template is bundled in the package (`template-registry.ts`: bundled is the only source), `latest` is `create-objectstack@18.6.0`, and that package carries the old `note` template with matching 18.6.0 pins. `create-objectstack` and `@objectstack/spec` are in one `fixed` group and publish together, so the new template first reaches a user with the 19 packages it needs.

Three costs are real:
- The getting-started pages on `main` (`your-first-project.mdx`, `build-with-claude-code.mdx`) describe companies and contacts, while `npm create objectstack` on `latest` keeps producing the `note` project until 19.0 GA, not only until the first prerelease. A reader following those pages sees a different tree and different curl targets.
- Anyone who runs the scaffolder from a checkout of `main` and installs from npm gets a project that does not load. `ObjectSchema.create` on 18.6.0 refuses `color`, then `fieldGroups[].fields` and object-form `relatedLists`, so validate, build, test and dev all fail at import. That is exactly the CI job's pairing; no published path produces it.
- Not measured on 18.6.0: `npm test` and the boot of the generated project. The dev measured validate only, with the three shapes stripped, and the CI job skips the later steps.

**2. The expected red.** `Scaffold with repo dist` is not in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` (11 contexts; none from `scaffold-e2e.yml`). The job log shows it red at step 7 only, with `✗ ObjectSchema.create('e2e_app_company'): unknown key(s) — color.`, after a registry install at 18.6.0; steps 1 to 6 passed. That is the reason §C gives. #37441 carries the fix (install from packed tarballs; acceptance: this head green on the job with no template change, plus a red control) and is open and unclaimed. The job has no push trigger, and the nightly leg of the workflow runs only the registry canary, so after the merge the red shows on pull requests that touch `packages/create-objectstack/**` or `docker/**`.

Check-runs on the head at 2026-11-26T09:14Z, 73 runs: nothing else is red. Green among the required contexts: Lint & Repo Gates, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate. Still running: Test Core shards 1 to 7 and 10 (8 and 9 green; the platform-objects sweeps are in 8), all Test UI shards but 12, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, and `Type Check · workspace`. So TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Test UI, Type Check UI and Build & E2E UI have no verdict yet. The PR is still a draft.

**3. The platform-objects edit.** It changes only the `SCAFFOLDING_TEMPLATES` list in the two sweeps and weakens nothing. The exemption stays an exact path list of files that are template payload and cannot be imported here; it goes from one file to two because the template now has two objects. The sweep still pins both ways (each listed path must exist; walked minus swept must equal the list length). Neither template object declares `enable.apiMethods`, `userActions` or a managed marker, so nothing the sweeps judge is taken out of their reach.

**4.** See S2 and S3: both need cards.

**5. Tests that pin the template.** The parity pin has a built-in CONTROL that cannot pass vacuously (if the mutation stops applying, the mutated text equals the Starter's and the control goes red) and vacuity guards on both namespaces and on each definition. The rewrite tests pin both directions: five reference shapes moved, four non-name shapes byte-identical. The dev's ablations are stated with counts (starter test 1 failed and 2 passed with the notes entry deleted; field-consumer controls 12, 7 and 0 red for the three helper widths; 14 red with a no-op helper). The nightly strip pattern in `starter-field-consumers.e2e.test.ts` depends on one-line groups, but a reformat makes its control red, not silent. The weak point is S1: the template's own `starter.test.ts` runs in no CI on this head.

### ② Semver level

`'create-objectstack': patch` is correct. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: the diff touches no file under `packages/spec`, and no key, value or type an author can write changes. `Clause-②: no` holds: `rewriteObjectNamePrefix` is internal to a bin package, the wider rewrite applies only while scaffolding a new project, and existing projects are untouched. The changeset body carries both declaration lines and says all three user-visible things (template content, the wider rename, the closing summary). `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/platform-objects` change in tests only and need no changeset; `Check Changeset` is green.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Declared deviation, the wider rewrite: accepted. It is what lets the template spell references as the Starter does, and both directions are pinned. N2 is its one blind spot.
- Fence additions (cli tests, docs pages, `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, `turbo.json`, the two platform-objects files): each has a claim amendment (7182121876, 7182284580) or the maintainer's 「改」, quoted in re-claim 7187337406 and read in the thread. `scaffold-e2e.yml` is not edited.
- The open question of report 7182719215 is answered: ruling 7183516548 (A with D), then the maintainer's 08:58Z word lifted the wait half; the Starter-identical source stands and D stays as #37441. That word answered a one-red cost; M1 was not in front of the maintainer.
- Out-of-scope findings of the report: the `scaffold-e2e.yml` comments go to #37441; the other two are S2 and S3.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- `main` has moved since the merge base (the Starter's config now reads `engines: { protocol: '^19' }`). The parity pin reads only the namespace line of that file and the Starter's `src/` is unchanged, so the pin holds on the merged tree.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-d9kjuz`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `973207caad6ea4b0cc064a1d29abc28222145f41`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5. Contract record 7187700473 (declaration face, `TIER_DEFAULT`) reads **FAIL** on M1. The template is Starter-identical as ruled, `requiresObject` is a correct guard, and the platform-objects edit weakens nothing.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 37 files (+898/−314), `Fixes #36945`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `create-objectstack` patch. Not governed. The maintainer overrode the wait on the card thread at 08:58Z (「你可以落地啊」, 「改」). At 09:14Z five required contexts were still running.
2. **Premise**: an `npm create objectstack` user pays nothing before the 19 publish. The published 18.6.0 scaffolder still bundles the old template, and the new one ships with the 19 packages in the same `fixed` group. The one expected red, "Scaffold with repo dist", is not required and is red only for §C's reason (`unknown key(s) — color`). #37441 carries it.
3. **Owed before ACCEPT**:
   - **M1.** The PR breaks a second gate that §C does not list. `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` (L1183–1211) reads `$APP_DIR/src/objects/note.object.ts` and POSTs `{"title":…}`. In pack mode the project comes from the repo-built scaffolder, so that file is gone and the script (`set -euo pipefail`) stops at the CRUD probes. That is `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` on the release branch, which runs after every Release run and is green today. The first 19.0.0-next cut is due now. Make the probe work in both modes, because registry mode still gets the 18.6.0 `note` template until 19.0 GA, and add the script to the claim. If a mode cannot be satisfied, list it in §C with a carrier.
   - **S1.** §C understates the window cost. The red job stops at step 7, so `starter.test.ts`, the boot probe, the skills, pinned-shape and Docker legs are all skipped, and no other CI job runs the template's test. State that in §C. Moving #37441 up is the maintainer's call; the seat asks.
   - **S2.** File a card: crediting an object-form related list's `columns` to the declaring object is a missed `os validate` / `os lint` finding, and `withoutPlacement` now masks it.
   - **S3.** File a family card: `generate.ts`'s "style is unchanged" comment is partly false (`os g object` writes per-field `group`), plus the stale `note` citations, including `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx:1091`.
   - The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations** (nits, record only):
   - N1: the "two-line" edit is two sites, +4/−2.
   - N2: the dotted-ref blind spot in the rewrite and its self-check.
   - N3: the parity pin holds the object set but not the view set.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**:
   - Scaffold E2E from packed tarballs: #37441.
   - S2 and S3: area-filed cards, under #36945.
   - Getting-started pages describing a tree `latest` does not produce until GA: name this in the S3 card.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. Owed: M1 closed, S1–S3 closed or carried, required contexts green, a same-head delta PASS and an **ACCEPT**. Then the area lands it with `--land`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `4bf5626c8c3c31086a4daee07ab7f5b1dce7997f`
Local-runs: none

PR #37428 (card #36945), declaration face, `Clause-②: no`. Delta round on the record for head 973207ca. Read: the delta `973207ca..4bf5626c` (two commits, two files: `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` and `packages/cli/test/create-objectstack-stack-reach.test.ts`), the whole diff against `origin/main` again (39 files, +936/−335), the PR body with the rewritten §C, the two new claim amendments on #36945 (7187718716, 7187834868), cards #37502, #37503 and #37441, the check-runs on this head and the failed job's log. The branch took no merge of `main` in this round (merge base still ee11fce9), so nothing from `main` touches an earlier finding. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Earlier findings**

- M1 (must-fix) — closed. `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` now picks the starter object by the file the scaffolder wrote: `company.object.ts` with `name`, else `note.object.ts` with `title`, else a named `fail`. The object name is still read from the generated source, and the first `name: '…'` in the template's `company.object.ts` is the object's own (line 25), so the read lands on the right literal. All four probes use the chosen object and field. Both modes are covered: pack mode gets the company branch, registry mode keeps the `note` branch until the companies template is published. Read from the script; the area's runs are as §C reports them (registry mode whole script exit 0; the company branch 201/200/200/200 against workspace packages; the old section exits 1 with ENOENT). `scripts/publish-smoke.sh` is in the fence by claim amendment 7187718716. See N4 for what is still unmeasured.
- S1 (should-fix) — closed for the text. §C now says what the red costs: steps 8 to 14 skipped, no CI job runs `starter.test.ts` or boots a generated project until #37441 lands or a 19 prerelease is published, on this PR and on later ones touching `packages/create-objectstack/**` or `docker/**`. The ordering half is carried by #37441, which is still `pm:queue`, p2 and unclaimed.
- S2 (should-fix) — carried by #37502 (open, sub-issue of #36945). The card states the defect, the measured control and the three done-when lines, including narrowing `withoutPlacement` back.
- S3 (should-fix) — carried by #37503 (open, sub-issue of #36945). It holds the `generate.ts` placement-dialect decision, the `cli.mdx` transcript, the stale comments, and the getting-started pages running ahead of `latest`.
- N1 (nit) — closed. Wording only; nothing owed.
- N2 (nit) — still open, no card. The rewrite pattern and its self-check stay blind to a dotted `'blank_contact.company'`. The template has none, and `objectstack validate` in the generated project would refuse one.
- N3 (nit) — still open, no card. The parity pin holds the object file set but not the view file set, and pins the closing summary by source text.

**New in this round**

- N4 (nit) — A full pack-mode run of `publish-smoke.sh` has not been done on this head; §C says so. `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)` is skipped. The company branch was measured as a cut-out section against workspace packages, not against packed tarballs. The first whole-script verdict will be the `publish-smoke / packed-tarballs` status after the merge. The opt-in label would give that verdict before the merge, at about 45 minutes.
- N5 (nit) — The PR body's Acceptance notes still say the field-consumer finding is "noted here, not filed" and that the style `generate.ts` describes "is unchanged". Both are now carried by #37502 and #37503; the notes should cite the cards.
- N6 (nit) — #37502 names the helper's file as `packages/create-objectstack/src/starter-field-consumers.test.ts`. The file is `packages/cli/test/starter-field-consumers.test.ts`.

**The stack-reach pin.** `create-objectstack-stack-reach.test.ts` now expects `Data: 3 Objects` (company, contact, and the object the test generates) where it expected 2. That is the template's new count and not a loosened assertion: the pattern is still an exact count, and `Logic: 1 Flows` is unchanged. The file is in the fence by claim amendment 7187834868. The earlier record missed this test because its shard had no verdict at the time of that read.

**The expected red.** `Scaffold with repo dist` (job 139810778450) fails at step 7 only, with `✗ ObjectSchema.create('e2e_app_company'): unknown key(s) — color.`, after steps 1 to 6 passed. That is the single reason §C names; nothing new is in the log. It is not in `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS`.

**Check-runs on this head at 2026-11-26T09:47Z, 71 runs:** 58 success, 10 skipped, 1 failure (the expected one), 2 still running: Test Core shards 3/10 and 5/10, both started 09:24Z. So the required context `Test Core` has no verdict yet.
